court: Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit

issues.label: Appellate jurisdiction and finality
issues.why: The court must confirm it has jurisdiction over an appeal from a final, appealable judgment.

issues.label: Standard of review: exhaustion
issues.why: The court must apply the correct standard of review to the PLRA exhaustion ruling and related fact findings.

issues.label: Standard of review: summary judgment
issues.why: The court must determine de novo whether summary judgment was proper and whether genuine disputes of material fact exist.

issues.label: Standard of review: 1915A dismissal
issues.why: The court must review de novo whether the complaint stated a claim under §1915A screening standards.

issues.label: Standard of review: reconsideration denial
issues.why: The court must identify the correct standard for reviewing denial of reconsideration of the §1915A order.

issues.label: Proper procedural vehicle used
issues.why: The court must address whether exhaustion was properly resolved on summary judgment without discovery and on the presented record.

issues.label: Burden of proof on exhaustion
issues.why: Because exhaustion is an affirmative defense, the court must ensure defendants carried the burden to prove non-exhaustion.

issues.label: What counts as ‘available’ remedies
issues.why: The court must determine whether the VDOC grievance process was actually available to Carter as required by Ross v. Blake.

issues.label: Effect of intake rejections
issues.why: The court must decide whether rejected-at-intake grievances (and appealed rejections) constitute proper exhaustion under VDOC rules.

issues.label: Exhaustion timing rule
issues.why: The court must decide whether exhaustion must be complete before the original complaint is filed or whether later exhaustion can suffice.

issues.label: Amended complaint curing defect
issues.why: The court must decide whether filing an amended complaint after exhaustion can cure an initially unexhausted action.

issues.label: Hardin v. Hunt applicability
issues.why: The court must determine whether and how an unpublished decision controls the cure-by-amendment question in this case.

issues.label: Relation-back implications
issues.why: The court must consider whether Rule 15(c) relation back affects the exhaustion timing analysis for claims first added in the amendment.

issues.label: Claim-by-claim exhaustion
issues.why: The court must decide whether PLRA exhaustion must be evaluated separately for each claim and each defendant.

issues.label: Exhaustion for new retaliation claim
issues.why: The court must determine whether the First Amendment retaliation claim (first pled in January 2023) was itself exhausted and when.

issues.label: Exhaustion for conditions claims
issues.why: The court must determine whether Carter exhausted grievances about RHU conditions before suit or before the operative complaint.

issues.label: Exhaustion as to Branch June complaint
issues.why: The court must decide whether Carter’s failure to file a regular grievance after the June 2022 informal complaint defeats exhaustion for that retaliation theory.

issues.label: Grievance content sufficiency
issues.why: The court must decide whether Carter’s grievances provided enough notice of the complained-of conduct and implicated defendants as required by prison rules.

issues.label: Effect of pending appeals at filing
issues.why: The court must decide whether filing while intake-appeals were pending is non-exhaustion or excusable if the process was effectively unavailable.

issues.label: Dismissal type for non-exhaustion
issues.why: If non-exhaustion exists, the court must decide whether dismissal should be without prejudice rather than with prejudice.

issues.label: Partial vs total dismissal
issues.why: The court must decide whether any exhausted claims may proceed even if others were unexhausted.

issues.label: Mootness of injunctive relief
issues.why: Because Carter left Sussex/RHU, the court must decide whether claims for injunctive relief are moot or fit an exception.

issues.label: Exception: capable of repetition
issues.why: The court must assess whether Carter is likely to be returned to Sussex/RHU such that injunctive claims remain justiciable.

issues.label: Exception: systemwide policy claim
issues.why: If relief targets VDOC-wide practices, the court must consider whether transfer moots claims against officials with statewide authority.

issues.label: Standing for prospective relief
issues.why: The court must ensure Carter has a real and immediate threat of future injury to support injunctive relief.

issues.label: Proper defendants for injunction
issues.why: The court must decide which officials, if any, have authority to implement prospective relief (e.g., current director/wardens).

issues.label: Commonwealth as §1983 defendant
issues.why: The court must address that a state is not a ‘person’ under §1983 and is generally immune from suit.

issues.label: Eleventh Amendment immunity
issues.why: The court must determine whether sovereign immunity bars damages and/or retrospective relief against the Commonwealth and official-capacity defendants.

issues.label: Official vs individual capacity
issues.why: The court must clarify capacities in which defendants are sued, affecting immunity, damages, and injunctive relief.

issues.label: Ex parte Young applicability
issues.why: The court must decide whether any official-capacity claim for prospective relief fits the Ex parte Young exception.

issues.label: Personal involvement requirement
issues.why: For individual-capacity §1983 liability, the court must decide whether each defendant’s actions are sufficiently alleged/shown.

issues.label: Supervisory liability standard
issues.why: The court must apply the correct Fourth Circuit standard for supervisory liability (knowledge, indifference, causation) as to Clarke.

issues.label: Clarke knowledge and notice
issues.why: The court must decide whether allegations about Porter, VDOC policies, or grievances plausibly show Clarke’s actual/constructive knowledge of Carter’s conditions.

issues.label: Causation for Clarke liability
issues.why: The court must assess whether any identified supervisory omissions by Clarke plausibly caused or perpetuated the unconstitutional conditions.

issues.label: PLRA physical-injury bar
issues.why: For mental/emotional injury damages, the court must consider 42 U.S.C. §1997e(e) and what damages remain available.

issues.label: Availability of nominal damages
issues.why: The court must decide whether nominal damages remain recoverable despite §1997e(e) and/or mootness of injunctive relief.

issues.label: Punitive damages prerequisites
issues.why: The court must determine whether allegations support reckless/evil intent sufficient for punitive damages if liability is shown.

issues.label: Eighth Amendment objective prong
issues.why: The court must decide whether RHU conditions alleged constitute a sufficiently serious deprivation or substantial risk of serious harm.

issues.label: Eighth Amendment subjective prong
issues.why: The court must decide whether defendants were deliberately indifferent to the risk posed by RHU conditions, especially given Carter’s mental illness.

issues.label: Porter v. Clarke comparability
issues.why: The court must determine how closely Carter’s RHU conditions match those deemed unconstitutional in Porter and whether distinctions matter.

issues.label: Mental illness vulnerability
issues.why: The court must consider whether Carter’s serious mental illnesses heighten the risk and affect deliberate-indifference analysis.

issues.label: Duration and severity of isolation
issues.why: The court must evaluate the length and intensity of segregation alleged, which is central to Eighth Amendment conditions claims.

issues.label: Qualified immunity (Eighth)
issues.why: The court must decide whether the Eighth Amendment right was clearly established for these officials at the relevant time.

issues.label: Protected First Amendment activity
issues.why: The court must decide whether informal complaints and grievances constitute protected speech/petitioning activity.

issues.label: Adverse action definition
issues.why: The court must decide whether denial of reentry/reclassification or continued RHU confinement would deter an ordinary inmate from protected activity.

issues.label: Causal connection for retaliation
issues.why: The court must decide whether Branch’s statements and timing plausibly show retaliatory motive and but-for causation.

issues.label: Legitimate penological reasons
issues.why: The court must consider whether defendants can show the same decision would have occurred absent protected activity for legitimate reasons.

issues.label: Retaliation personal involvement
issues.why: The court must decide whether McCoy and Cabell personally participated in or directed retaliation or can be liable on a plausible theory.

issues.label: Retaliation plausibility vs proof stage
issues.why: The court must ensure the correct standard was used (pleading vs evidentiary) given the court analyzed retaliation under Rule 12(b)(6) while granting summary judgment.

issues.label: Qualified immunity (retaliation)
issues.why: The court must decide whether the retaliation right was clearly established and whether a reasonable official could think the conduct lawful.

issues.label: PLRA exhaustion for retaliation grievance
issues.why: The court must assess whether the late-September 2022 retaliation grievance properly exhausted that claim and whether its rejection/appeal affects exhaustion.

issues.label: PLRA exhaustion for conditions grievance
issues.why: The court must assess whether the late-September 2022 conditions grievance properly exhausted those claims and whether rejection/appeal completion suffices.

issues.label: Effect of grievance screening rules
issues.why: The court must determine whether VDOC screening requirements (timeliness, form, subject-matter limits) were properly applied and whether improper screening makes remedies unavailable.

issues.label: Evidentiary record on exhaustion
issues.why: The court must decide whether the record conclusively established grievance dates, content, rejection reasons, and appeal outcomes.

issues.label: Opportunity for discovery
issues.why: The court must consider whether summary judgment before discovery was appropriate given exhaustion and merits depend on institutional records and officials’ knowledge.

issues.label: Proper disposition of mixed claims
issues.why: The court must decide whether to sever/dismiss only unexhausted claims and proceed on exhausted ones, consistent with Jones v. Bock principles.

issues.label: Statute of limitations concerns
issues.why: If dismissal without prejudice is required, the court must consider limitations and tolling implications under §1983 borrowing rules.

issues.label: PLRA filing-fee/IFP effects
issues.why: The court must ensure procedural compliance with PLRA/IFP provisions does not affect jurisdiction or the propriety of dismissal grounds.

issues.label: Naming ‘unnamed officials’
issues.why: The court must consider whether claims against John/Jane Doe officials can proceed and the effect of amendment/service timing.

issues.label: Service and participation of parties
issues.why: The court must verify proper service and whether all defendants were properly before the court when rulings were made.

issues.label: Relief scope under §1983
issues.why: The court must ensure requested relief (damages, injunction) is legally available against each defendant given immunity and mootness constraints.
